topic: White House launches arcade games promoting Trump policies amid Iran war and economic crisis
tweet1: The White House unveiled five arcade games promoting Trump policies—Flappy Bill, Build the Wall, Rio Run—while gas prices hit $4/gallon, Iran war drags on, and midterms loom.
tweet2: @AJEnglish reports critics accuse the administration of "prioritising entertainment over rising costs and foreign wars." @RT_com lists the games: Tetris-style wall builder, Snake-style border runner. This is official WH output during an actual shooting war.
tweet3: @AJEnglish quotes Trita Parsi warning Iran could "time the conflict to hurt Trump politically" with oil at $97/barrel. The White House response: browser games. Not a press conference on Hormuz. Not an inflation plan. Flappy Bird.
tweet4: This is what governance collapse looks like: arcade games as policy communication while a blockade fails and Americans pay $4/gallon. Prediction: post-midterm Trump acts more recklessly, per Parsi's warning, because distraction stopped working.
